liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Greatest Story Ever Told** (2 reviews): Jerry is in top form throughout Greatest Story Ever Told; Reviewer, normally not a fan of this song, finds this version great [15][16]
- **He's Gone** (2 reviews): The He's Gone through Spanish Jam stretch is the heart of the show, with Jerry and Phil standing out; He's Gone through Casey Jones is about fifty minutes of lyrical, jazzy jamming [6][13]
- **The Other One** (2 reviews): The Other One and the jams that follow it are singled out as outstanding; The Other One jam into I Know You Rider is praised for groovy playing [7][15]
- **El Paso** (1 review): El Paso is likewise singled out as great [16]
- **They Love Each Other** (1 review): Played in a faster style the band later dropped; reviewer finds it superb [9]
- **Playing in the Band** (1 review): The Playing in the Band that follows is called monumental [9]
- **Casey Jones** (1 review): During Casey Jones, a three-story locomotive front was revealed from behind the curtain [11]

## The recordings

- **gd73-03-31.sbd.yerys.2237.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 166 min; rated 4.22/5 by 41 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound is good though not the best; it works well enough; Reviewer calls the sound quality fabulous; Sound is excellent for 1973, graded B+/A [1][6][9][13]
- **gd1973-03-31.sbd.hamilton.2986.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 26 songs; 166 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [2]. Said about its sound: The etree copy's track boundaries often began thirty seconds to a minute before songs actually started [2]
- **gd1973-03-31.sbd.bertha-ashley.31604.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 24 songs; 166 min; rated 4.15/5 by 13 [3]. Said about its sound: Many rough transitions between songs, apparently from a tape machine stopping and starting [3]
- **gd1973-03-31.172511.sbd.flegel.flac1644**: soundboard; 22 songs; 166 min [4]. Said about its sound: First set had many dropouts and cuts, which were smoothed with crossfades and patches [4]

## Around the show

- An attendee recalls a mirror ball switched on during a jam while Jerry left the stage [11]
- The band tuned up with a bit of Beer Barrel Polka, split across discs two and three [2]
- Lacks some favorite 1973 pieces, such as Dark Star and China>Rider, yet the reviewer returns to it often [5]
- Jerry's tone is strong here and at the 21st and 26th March shows [10]
- The playing resembles the late June run that followed that year [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd73-03-31.sbd.yerys.2237.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: The reviewer's old cassette copy held only He's Gone through Casey Jones; Master soundboard reel to cassette to DAT to CD-R, via Morgan Evans and Ben Yerys [1][13]
- **gd1973-03-31.sbd.hamilton.2986.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by EAC Morgan Evans, retracking by G.S. Hamilton; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Original etree info file's lineage is wrong; uploader retracked the whole show using Cool Edit and CDWav [2]
- **gd1973-03-31.sbd.bertha-ashley.31604.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Jay Ashley and Gary Field; source: SBD > MC > CASS > DAT > CDA > DAW(Bertha) > Audio DVD > DVD Audio Extractor v.3.3.2 (audio files extracted prior to burning to DVD disc) > 24/48 wav >… [3]. Also: Remastered November 9, 2005 on a dual-DAW system nicknamed Bertha; spectral analysis shows two analog generations, likely cassette master to cassette [3]
- **gd1973-03-31.172511.sbd.flegel.flac1644**: source: Embellishment of prior partial soundboard (Morgan Evans) by Brian Fegel [4]. Also: Converted the Hamilton shn files and patched in GD 320 tracks from He's Gone through I Know You Rider [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Richard Manning: [1973–Buffalo Memorial Auditorium-Grateful Dead Concert Poster-Artist Owned Copy- SIGNED! RARE FIRST PRINTING! PAE Graded](https://results.concertpostergallery.com/lot/10575) [18]
